VI._name: SoundVib_MCM Examples.lvlib:Order Tracking Magnitude and Phase (Analog Tach, DAQmx).vi
VI.description: This VI demonstrates how to compute order magnitude and phase. This VI uses DAQmx VIs to acquire sound or vibration signals and an analog tachometer signal and displays order magnitude and phase results continuously. \0A\0AINSTRUCTIONS\3A\0A1. On the DAQ Configurations page\2C specify the device and channel configurations\2C time settings\2C and tachometer channel information.\0A2. On the Magnitude and Phase page\2C specify the orders to compute\2C view\2C magnitude view\2C and x-axis selection to get the desired order magnitude and phase display. \0A3. Run the VI.\0A4. On the Magnitude and Phase page\2C select the signal of interest in the select channel control.\0A\0AVIs USED IN THIS EXAMPLE\3A\0A1.\09OAT Analog Tacho Process.vi\0A2.\09OAT Convert to Even Angle Signal.vi\0A3.\09OAT Order Magnitude and Phase.vi\0A4.\09SVL Unit Conversion.vi

Control.description: orders to compute specifies the orders to use to compute the magnitude and phase. The default is 1.00.

bandwidth specifies an order span centered at the order that you specify in orders to compute. Use a bandwidth [order] value between 0 and 1. If bandwidth [order] is less than 0 or greater than 1\2C this VI sets bandwidth [order] to 1. The default is 1.00.
X axis selection specifies the type of scale the VI uses for the x-axis of the output XY plot.
magnitude view specifies the peak scaling of the converted spectrum.
view specifies the view settings for the magnitudes [RMS] and the phases [phase lag].
time/speed segment specifies the settings for dividing the input XY signal into segments. The scale type you specified in x-axis selection determines the unit of segment settings.

FreeLabel.comment: Key Concepts\3A\0A\0AA. Using resampling to correlate the vibration signal with the rotational speed allows for this example to be used for online analysis.

For more information on specific functions\3A Show Context Help <Ctrl+H>\0A\0ASteps\3A\0A1. Use the DAQmx AI Config XControl to configure DAQ channel properties and start the DAQmx task.\0A2. Specifies sample mode and reads input block size with the Timing Node.\0A3. Use the DAQmx Read VI to measure multiple samples from channels on the device.\0A4. Separates the tachometer waveform from the vibration waveform and gets specific waveform attributes. \0A5. Determines the tachometer pulse positions and generates a speed profile.\0A6. Resamples the vibration signal from an even-time-spaced signal to even-angle-spaced signal.\0A7. Calculates the magnitude and phase of the provided even-angle signal for the requested orders.\0A8. Select the order magnitudes and phases of the specified channel and set the magnitude view.\0A9. Converts input data to desired units.\0A10. Prepares data to be displayed in either even-time or even-speed intervals based on the input X-axis selection and the input segment settings. \0A11. Buffers the signal to display historical data as well as current data.\0A12. Call the DAQmx Clear Task VI to clear the Task.
